transcript: Speaker A: Typing breaks your flow state. Here's what I do instead. You're deep in a session, you see the whole feature in your head, the logic, the structure, all of it. Then you stop to type a prompt. And that 30 seconds of typing, your brain switches gears. You go from building mode to transcription mode. And by the time you hit enter, half the ideas are already fuzzy. I noticed this happening to me in every single session. So, I stopped typing my prompts entirely. Now, I just talk. Wispr Flow captures it and drops it right into Cursor, Claude, wherever I'm working. Now, my brain stays in building mode. The idea comes out whole, not in fragments. Try Wispr Flow for free and thank me later.

summary: The presenter explains how typing out prompts disrupts his coding flow state by switching his brain from building to transcription mode. He demonstrates using Wispr Flow, a voice-to-text tool that captures spoken ideas and inputs them directly into coding environments like Cursor or Claude. He invites viewers to try Wispr Flow for free to maintain their creative momentum.
